 Coastal storm could bring eastern Pa. severe weather, maybe even snow, this week

 A pedestrian uses an umbrella to keep dry as they walk Sunday, Feb. 22, 2026, as the weather changed from rain to flurries in Bethlehem. (April Gamiz/The Morning Call) 
 By Leif Greiss | lgreiss@mcall.com | The Morning Call PUBLISHED: November 8, 2026 at 10:59 AM EST | UPDATED: November 8, 2026 at 2:50 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... A coastal system is “increasingly likely” to impact eastern Pennsylvania and the surrounding region later this week, according to the National Weather Service.
 There is still a lot of uncertainty surrounding the potential storm, the weather service cautions, but it has the potential to bring as much as 2-3 inches of rain, with even a small chance of snow.
 A low pressure system is expected to develop by late Wednesday over the Ohio Valley, then track east. By Friday, it is expected to be off the mid-Atlantic coast, where it will strengthen, according to the weather service’s Weather Prediction Center.
 Our region could feel the impacts of the storm starting Thursday and continuing through Friday night, according to the weather service.
 “It’s not looking like a big snowstorm, more in the way of rain with potentially some snow. It’s not looking like a big snowstorm,” said Paul Fitzsimmons, a meteorologist with the weather service’s Mount Holly, N.J., forecast office.
 If the system does produce snow, it it is most likely over higher elevations, according to the weather service. The weather service cautions that it’s too early to tell just how much snow could occur, and whether there will be any over lower elevations.
 A map shared by the Weather Prediction Center showed much of eastern Pennsylvania — including the Lehigh Valley, Berks County and the Philadelphia region — at roughly a 10 percent chance of seeing at least 1 inch of snow between Thursday and Saturday evening. Portions of northeastern Pennsylvania, including the Poconos, were showing slightly higher probabilities.
 After the storm moves out, colder than average temperatures will move in through next weekend.
 The rest of the week is expected to be relatively clear. For Sunday, the weather service is calling for partly sunny conditions that give way to sunny weather later in the day with a high in the low 60s. Westward winds could yield gusts of up to 20 mph.
 Sunday evening is expected to be mostly clear and cool at 41 degrees with gentle western winds of up to 10 mph.
 Here is the rest of this week’s forecast:
 Monday: Mostly sunny, with a high near 60. Northwest wind 10 to 15 mph, with gusts up to 30 mph.
 Monday night: Partly cloudy, with a low around 37. West wind around 5 mph.
 Tuesday: Sunny, with a high near 63. West wind 5 to 10 mph, with gusts up to 20 mph.
 Tuesday night: Clear, with a low around 38.
 Wednesday, Veterans Day: Sunny, with a high near 63.
 Wednesday night: Partly cloudy, with a low around 37.
 Thursday: A chance of rain after 1 p.m. Mostly cloudy, with a high near 56. Chance of precipitation is 50%.
 Thursday night: A chance of rain. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 32. Chance of precipitation is 50%.
 Friday: A chance of rain. Mostly cloudy, with a high near 49. Chance of precipitation is 40%.
